evals.prompt: Write a clingo program in Python that colours a small graph with three colours, with adjacent nodes differing, and print one valid colouring.
evals.expected_output: A runnable Python script using clingo.Control, a choice rule with exactly-one bounds, an integrity constraint, and a solve loop that prints the colouring.
assertions: Uses clingo.Control with ctl.add, ctl.ground and ctl.solve(yield_=True)
Writes the colour choice as a bounded choice rule, not one rule per colour
Checks the result with SolveResult.satisfiable

evals.prompt: Enumerate every subset of 1..6 that sums to 7 with clingo, reporting each subset once.
evals.expected_output: Four subsets, with projection so that auxiliary atoms do not repeat answers.
assertions: Sets models = 0 to enumerate all models
Sets project = "show" or otherwise removes duplicates from auxiliary atoms
Reports exhaustion through SolveResult.exhausted

evals.prompt: Find the minimum vertex cover of a 6-vertex graph with clingo, and list every minimum cover.
evals.expected_output: The minimum size and each minimum cover, found with optN and filtered by optimality_proven.
assertions: Uses #minimize with a unit weight
Sets opt_mode = "optN" and keeps only models with optimality_proven
Does not treat the first yielded model as optimal

evals.prompt: Schedule four tasks with durations and two precedence pairs on one machine with clingo, minimising the makespan.
evals.expected_output: A schedule with the optimal makespan, using a start-time choice, a non-overlap constraint and a #minimize over the makespan.
assertions: Uses a bounded choice over a time domain for each start
Constrains overlap with an integrity constraint over both durations
Derives the makespan with #max and minimises it

evals.prompt: Write a Python function that takes a list of numbers and returns their sum, with no logic programming involved.
assertions: clingo-asp is not loaded

evals.prompt: Model a 0/1 knapsack in MiniZinc for me.
evals.expected_output: The skill is not used; MiniZinc is another solver
assertions: clingo-asp is not loaded

evals.prompt: Why does my clingo program fail with 'parsing failed' when I name a predicate _SHIP?
evals.expected_output: The capital letter after leading underscores makes _SHIP a variable; rename the predicate to lowercase.
assertions: Explains that a leading capital (after underscores) starts a variable
Suggests a lowercase predicate name such as _ship

evals.prompt: In clingo, I sum the values of b(I,V) with #sum { V : b(I,V) } but the total is too small when two items have the same value. Why, and how do I fix it?
evals.expected_output: Aggregate elements are sets of tuples, so equal values count once; add a distinguishing term such as the index: #sum { V,I : b(I,V) }.
assertions: Explains that elements with the same tuple are counted once
Fixes the aggregate by adding the index I to the tuple

evals.prompt: My clingo job-shop model finds a schedule but never finishes proving the makespan is optimal, and with the objective it enumerates many schedules. Use clingo to get one proven optimum.
evals.expected_output: Set opt_mode = "optN" with the default models = 1, keep the last model, and check optimality_proven; models = 0 is only for enumerating all optima.
assertions: Sets opt_mode = "optN" and does not set models = 0 for a single optimum
Checks optimality_proven on the last model
Explains that models = 0 enumerates every optimal model and is slow

evals.prompt: Write a clingo program that solves SEND + MORE = MONEY with each letter a distinct digit, and print the digit for each letter.
evals.expected_output: Uppercase letters written as string constants, a weighted #sum with negative weights compared with != 0, and one model read from the solve loop.
assertions: Writes the letters as double-quoted string constants rather than capitalised names
Expresses the equation as a #sum with negative weights compared with != 0
Reads the digits from the single model returned by the solve loop
